claims.claim: Tyrion is an actual dwarf, a joke to passers-by, not a hearty axe-wielding fantasy dwarf.
claims.source: Lev Grossman, 'G.R.R. Martin's Complex Epic for an Ambivalent Age', NPR, 7 Jul 2011

claims.claim: Martin is a tense, surging, insomnia-inflicting plotter.
claims.source: Lev Grossman, 'The American Tolkien', Time, 13 Nov 2005

claims.claim: Martin is a deft and inexhaustible sketcher of personalities.
claims.source: Lev Grossman, 'The American Tolkien', Time, 13 Nov 2005
claims.quote: a deft and inexhaustible sketcher of personalities

claims.claim: Martin shoots the action from many angles with a dozen narrators to reflect its many-sided nature.
claims.source: Lev Grossman, 'The American Tolkien', Time, 13 Nov 2005
claims.quote: shoots the action from many angles, with a dozen narrators

claims.claim: It is men and women slugging it out in the muck for money, power, lust and love, not elves against orcs.
claims.source: Lev Grossman, 'The American Tolkien', Time, 13 Nov 2005
claims.quote: men and women slugging it out in the muck

claims.claim: Tolkien has imaginative force but one must go elsewhere for moral complexity; Martin's wars are multifaceted and ambiguous.
claims.source: Lev Grossman, 'The American Tolkien', Time, 13 Nov 2005
claims.quote: you have to go elsewhere for moral complexity

claims.claim: Tolkien was never so ponderous nor so obsessed with bodily functions (the Grand Maester befouling himself).
claims.source: Kirkus Reviews, 'A Dance with Dragons', 26 Sep 2011
claims.quote: Tolkien was never quite so ponderous

claims.claim: Book five is cynical, dark, with few laughs and not much action, mostly exposition.
claims.source: Kirkus Reviews, 'A Dance with Dragons', 26 Sep 2011
claims.quote: a little cynical, plenty dark, with not many laughs

claims.claim: Jon Snow's chapters go 'all Hamlety', soliciting input and keeping his own counsel.
claims.source: Kirkus Reviews, 'A Dance with Dragons', 26 Sep 2011
claims.quote: comes over all Hamlety, wondering what to do

claims.claim: On the evidence one wonders whether Martin is getting tired of the series.
claims.source: Kirkus Reviews, 'A Dance with Dragons', 26 Sep 2011
claims.quote: one wonders if Martin isn’t getting a little tired

claims.claim: The series is told through an array of constantly shifting perspectives across many locales.
claims.source: Bill Sheehan, 'A Dance with Dragons worth the long long wait', Washington Post, 12 Jul 2011 (read via Wayback)
claims.quote: an array of constantly shifting perspectives

claims.claim: Vividly rendered set pieces, cliffhangers and appalling cruelty make it epic fantasy as it should be written.
claims.source: Bill Sheehan, 'A Dance with Dragons worth the long long wait', Washington Post, 12 Jul 2011 (read via Wayback)
claims.quote: passionate, compelling, convincingly detailed and thoroughly imagined

claims.claim: The book feels grounded in brutal medieval reality, closer to the Wars of the Roses than to Lord of the Rings.
claims.source: Bill Sheehan, 'A Dance with Dragons worth the long long wait', Washington Post, 12 Jul 2011 (read via Wayback)
claims.quote: grounded in the brutal reality of medieval times

claims.claim: Characters repeatedly remind the reader that 'Winter is coming'.
claims.source: Bill Sheehan, 'A Dance with Dragons worth the long long wait', Washington Post, 12 Jul 2011 (read via Wayback)
claims.quote: as the characters repeatedly remind us

claims.claim: Martin writes as convincingly of tart apple juice as of mountain sleet; the book is an adventure of the senses.
claims.source: Paul Levinson, review of A Game of Thrones, Tangent #16, Fall 1996 (author's 2011 repost)
claims.quote: tart juices oozing from an apple as of sleet
